slides.callout: Different data, labels and splits prevent direct comparison of published percentages.
slides.notes: Sen et al.: CricShotClassify, Sensors 21(8), 2846 (2021), https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/8/2846 . CNN frame features and GRU, including frozen and partly fine-tuned VGG16 variants. Kang: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09187 , a preprint comparing sequence models and proposing EfficientNet-B0 with bidirectional GRU and temporal attention. No code or datasets from either paper were imported. KUCricShot authors' repository https://github.com/AtanuCSE/CricketShotDetection describes a separate four-shot, 1278-example dataset, also unused. Lecture 8 part 2 p9 distinguishes local/global features. Lecture 14 part 2 pp2-3 and 27 covers extractor/classifier and softmax. We implement an image comparison, not a new backbone or a priority claim.

slides.title: Implemented pipeline
slides.subtitle: Only the small cricket classifiers learn from the training images
slides.callout: Central crop assumes a centered batter. It can remove the bat or useful scene context.
slides.notes: Explain the two branches. HOG and CNN global inputs have identical aspect-preserving 224 square geometry. The fixed crop reduces some background without training a detector, but can miss an off-center batter. Keeping the global view preserves a second source of context, although square center fitting also removes peripheral pixels. MobileNetV2 is an efficient ImageNet backbone selected for CPU use; freezing limits cricket fitting to small heads on only 221 training groups. This is design reasoning, not proof that freezing or this model is optimal. CNN has two view passes; its heads share features. Source: actual implemented pipeline, https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04381 , and docs/course_mapping.md.

slides.title: HOG: gradients, cells and blocks
slides.subtitle: Lecture 10: accumulate gradient magnitude in orientation bins
slides.callout: Votes use magnitude, not frequency. No learned feature scaling; no test-based HOG tuning.
slides.notes: Trace gx and gy central differences, sqrt(gx²+gy²), atan2 modulo 180. A 50-degree gradient of magnitude 90 votes 45 to the 40-degree bin and 45 to 60. No spatial vote interpolation. Each 36-value block divides by sqrt(sum(h²)+1e-10). 13*13*36=6084. This is a documented HOG variant, not the exact signed-angle lecture example or original pedestrian detector. Lecture 10 pp 7-23; original method https://lear.inrialpes.fr/people/triggs/pubs/Dalal-cvpr05.pdf .

slides.title: CNN views and the contrast feature
slides.subtitle: Frozen ImageNet MobileNetV2 gives two 1,280-value pooled embeddings

blocks.text:
Absolute difference is nonlinear; signed difference would be redundant
for a linear head on concatenation. This motivates a test, not a success claim.

slides.notes: Both vectors are L2-normalized before joining so their raw magnitudes do not set the relative block scale; the joined descriptor is normalized again. Equal norm does not imply equal usefulness. No normalization ablation was conducted. A linear head on concatenation can compute signed u-v but cannot generally compute abs(u-v); the explicit block supplies this nonlinear relation. This is the motivation to test, not proof of improvement. Contrast W has (4,3840) shape plus four biases, 15364 stored parameters, trained with weighted multiclass cross-entropy and L2 regularization. No bat-motion interpretation is assigned to coordinates. MobileNetV2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04381 ; weights: https://github.com/onnx/models .

slides.title: Recognition results
slides.subtitle: Same corrected split; every test image contributes, including review cases
slides.callout: HOG is a controlled baseline. Pretrained features help here; contrast adds only three correct images.
slides.notes: HOG fixed settings, validation-selected C and predictions are saved under results/hog. Do not try a new descriptor after seeing the 35.3% test score to improve a headline. CNN heads/predictions are retained unchanged. This comparison does not isolate color versus pretraining versus architecture; no general statement that all HOG methods are inferior. Evidence: results/revision/comparison.csv and saved individual probabilities.

slides.title: Where contrast changes decisions
slides.subtitle: 17 concatenation errors corrected, but 14 correct decisions lost

blocks.text:
Selected examples: drive image_00696 is corrected;
drive image_00017 changes from correct to incorrect.

slides.callout: Paired group interval: -1.46 to +2.38 points. A reliable gain is not established.
slides.notes: This descriptive analysis uses unchanged saved test predictions. Cases are first IDs in gain/loss categories, selected after evaluation. image_00696: label drive; global drive, crop pull, concat pull, contrast drive. image_00017: label drive; global drive, crop glance/flick, concat drive, contrast glance/flick. Agreement subsets do not identify a causal mechanism or validate a new selection rule. For uncertainty, resample the 70 visual groups, retaining all their images, in 2000 paired draws with seed17; image-weighted statistics. The interval omits training/split variability and unknown match correlation. Complete individual-method intervals remain in report and results/revision/comparison.json; case evidence is in view_diagnostics.json.

slides.title: Class errors
slides.subtitle: Contrast confusion counts; rows are dataset labels
slides.callout: Macro F1 averages the four class F1 scores equally. Review does not remove mistakes from this table.
slides.notes: Read an off-diagonal entry and explain precision versus recall. Glance/flick is difficult under this protocol. HOG predicts pull for 110 of 224 sweep images. Fixed geometry, similar stances and background are plausible issues, not proven causes for each error. Evidence: saved prediction arithmetic in comparison.json.

slides.title: Scores, calibration and secondary review
slides.subtitle: Temperature scaling worsened the recorded test calibration

blocks.text:
Confidence alone
62.2% coverage / 77.6% accuracy
With agreement
58.9% coverage / 77.7% accuracy

Agreement rejects more images for negligible accuracy benefit.
Keep T = 0.802 and threshold = 0.70 unchanged.

slides.callout: Softmax is a relative class score. Agreement is not a guarantee or an unknown-shot detector.
slides.notes: NLL and ECE worsen. ECE uses ten equal-width confidence bins. The same validation set selected C, temperature and threshold; the 90% validation target did not transfer to test. The gate needs global/crop/contrast agreement; the heads are correlated. It accepts557/945 with433 correct. Its measured benefit over confidence alone is tiny. Retain it as visible triage for conflicting views; diagnostic heads use the same two encoder outputs, adding no encoder pass. HOG scores are unscaled and do not affect review. Sources: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500 .

slides.notes: Use image_04199, the preserved confident failure. Do not invent its exact cause or silently relabel it. The selected picture is an illustration, not an estimate of failure frequency. Real data source: aneesh10/cricket-shot-dataset v2. Follow with the view-disagreement image_00014.

Five shipped JPEG illustrations cover all four successful class labels plus confident error image_04199. The full local package also has original disagreement image_00014; public clones can restore it optionally. Fresh scores are computed from actual input files; JPEG inputs may differ from original benchmark pixels. All examples were selected after evaluation. Show actual views and HOG, then export JSON. Screenshot source is the running app.

slides.title: What we can defend
slides.subtitle: An implemented comparison with useful negative findings

blocks.text: HOG and frozen features, each followed by a trained multiclass head.

Explicit spatial-view difference, tested against concatenation.
17 decisions gained and 14 lost, with no reliable advantage.

slides.callout: Next useful step: independently labeled data with known match and player identities.
slides.notes: The implemented contribution is the controlled comparison and inspectable integration of two-view absolute differences and diagnostic agreement. Components are established; HOG itself is not new. The measured gain is uncertain, so do not claim a new architecture, detector or state-of-the-art result. The audit also corrects an optimistic initial result, and calibration fails to transfer. Mention possible missed copies and unverified labels. Course mapping and viva guide contain page references and a measured trace. Team identities and repository URL are on the cover.

slides.notes: Use only for questions. Equal 30.2% majority accuracy means weak video recognition, despite higher macro F1. Fixed crop followed pilot test feedback. Source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/amittalmale/cricket-shots . Image audit: pHash <=6 bits with thumbnail MAD, rotations/mirrors, then 15 feature neighbors within cosine .20. ORB binary matching, .72 ratio, >=16 matches, >=12 RANSAC inliers, >=65% inlier fraction, >=8% hull coverage. These are evaluation tools, not a novel shot classifier. Other sources: https://github.com/onnx/models ; https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn ; https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime ; https://github.com/opencv/opencv ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.00859 .
